Housing splits between the pre-1900 historic-downtown core, 1900s-1980s small-town residential blocks surrounding the courthouse square, and the dominant 1990s-2020s subdivision tier that accounts for most of McDonough's current residential footprint.

McDonough.wildlife_intro: McDonough's wildlife profile combines the small pre-1900 historic-downtown housing density around the 1823-founded Henry County Courthouse square with the dominant 1990s-2020s subdivision growth driven by the I-75 corridor commerce. Pre-1900 chimney stock around the courthouse square hosts long-established big-brown-bat (Eptesicus fuscus) colonies — some spanning 50-80+ years of continuous occupation. The I-75 corridor commercial clusters at McDonough Exit 218 and Exit 216 produce dense food-subsidy concentrations that elevate baseline raccoon and Norway rat activity in adjacent residential blocks. Most McDonough residential property sits in 1990s-2020s subdivision construction with builder-grade material failure profiles at gable vents, soffit transitions, and chimney chase caps. Eastern gray squirrels dominate residential calls; fox squirrels appear in rural-acreage edge properties. Roof rats are firmly established in McDonough subdivision canopy because of I-75 corridor establishment.

faqs.a: McDonough pre-1900 historic-district wildlife jobs run $700-$1,900+ because of multi-entry antebellum housing profiles. I-75 corridor-adjacent residential jobs run $450-$1,400+ depending on commercial-cluster food-subsidy pressure. 1990s-2020s subdivision jobs track $400-$1,300+. faqs.q: Are McDonough historic properties wildlife-prone?
faqs.a: Yes. Pre-1900 McDonough housing around the Henry County Courthouse square features original masonry chimneys without modern caps, hand-laid brick foundations, pre-modern wood soffits with corner separation, and brick-veneer separation. Multi-entry profiles (4-5 per property) are the rule on courthouse-square antebellum properties.

faqs.q: Are I-75 corridor properties hit harder by rats?
faqs.a: Yes. The I-75 commercial cluster at McDonough Exit 218 and Exit 216 concentrates fast-food restaurants, hotels, and gas stations in a small area. The food-service waste streams sustain heavy Norway rat source populations that disperse into adjacent residential blocks year-round.

faqs.q: Why do my 1990s McDonough subdivision soffits keep failing?
faqs.a: Builder-grade vinyl-soffit installations 25-35 years old commonly show corner separation at fascia-meet points. Original-installation tolerances plus decades of expansion-and-contraction produce the standard 1990s-subdivision multi-entry profile that drives squirrel, raccoon, and bat work.

faqs.q: Is service Georgia DNR-licensed?
faqs.a: Yes. All commercial wildlife trapping in McDonough requires a Georgia DNR Trapping License. Henry County falls in Georgia DNR Region 1 (Northeast) because of its Piedmont position. Pre-1900 chimney bat work additionally requires federal tricolored bat ESA-compliance documentation.

Hampton.wildlife_intro: Hampton's wildlife profile is distinctively shaped by Atlanta Motor Speedway — the major NASCAR venue that drives sharp event-week commercial pressure spikes during race weekends.
